articles.detail: 5 cycles, all completed; avg 10 published per cycle; 0 quarantined

experiment: Skipped. No experiment is active, every metric is within target, and the pause gate (`noNewExperimentsUntil` 2026-11-05) bars a new one. Nothing was evaluated or changed.
weakestArea: Science met its floor exactly at 5 for a second day, and politics took 23 of 50 stories (46%) while economy fell to 12 from 15. Sci-tech held at 30% only because tech carried 10; one science story (NASA's Artemis plan) is closer to space policy than research.
watching: Hormuz: Brent above $116, Iran's offer to reopen the strait against the US blockade, four states demanding reopening, and the US pulling diplomats from the Gulf.
Houthi strikes on Aden and Saudi sites, widening the Gulf escalation into Yemen.
A magnitude-7 earthquake in Xizang that has killed at least 16.
Ebola preparedness in Lagos after the Bundibugyo cases in Nigeria.
Brazil's runoff: Telegram channels spreading ballot doubts and questions over the Supreme Court's docket.
China's AI race: Moonshot undercutting GPT-6 Astra on price while accused of hidden promotion, and DeepSeek and Kimi diverging.
coverageGaps: Twelve datelines are a country rather than a city (China ×4, Brazil ×3, United States ×3, Nigeria, South Africa), up from nine yesterday; the missing-dateline metric does not catch them.
Oceania carried no story, the first zero in the window; the region floor still holds at five.
Four stories rest only on state or advocacy sources, three of them Hormuz stories leaning on Iranian and Gulf outlets.
context: Volume fell to 50 from 60 with all five cycles completing at about 10 published each. Multi-source rose to 34% from 33%, US datelines fell to 10% and Latin America rose to 18%. Cycles averaged 950s: selector 139s, writer 137s, editor 56s.
